section: Educational Psychology · Ch12 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Cerebral palsy is a condition primarily affecting a child's:

options.option_text: Muscle coordination and movement, due to a brain injury before/during/shortly after birth

explanation: Cerebral palsy results from brain injury affecting motor control and coordination; intelligence is often unaffected, though it varies by individual — it is not primarily a sensory or digestive condition.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch12 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A child who understands language well but has significant difficulty forming clear, fluent speech (e.g. stuttering) has a:

options.option_text: Speech disorder (expressive difficulty), distinct from a language comprehension disorder

explanation: Speech disorders (like stuttering) affect the physical production of speech, while comprehension may remain intact — distinct from language disorders (difficulty understanding/using language itself).

section: Educational Psychology · Ch12 — Special Needs & Inclusive Education
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A child who displays persistent, extreme aggression across multiple settings (home, school), well beyond typical age-appropriate behaviour, may be showing signs of an:

options.option_text: Emotional and behavioural disorder requiring professional assessment
Ordinary phase requiring no attention at all
Purely academic learning disability with no emotional component

explanation: Persistent, cross-setting, severe behavioural difficulty (beyond normal developmental variation) may indicate an emotional/behavioural disorder warranting professional evaluation and support, not dismissal as 'just a phase'.
